title: Our Humble Tribute to Our Humble Friend, Kiko
primary_topics: Eulogy delivered at the online Mass for the passing of Brother Francisco 'Kiko' Josef, a founding member of the BLD Old Treasury Ministry (OTM), May 16, 2021
Tribute to Kiko as the ideal worker in the Lord's vineyard -- embodying Matthew 25 in quiet, unobtrusive service
History of the BLD Old Treasury Ministry (OTM) / Support Services Center: 13 couple-members who built the BLD Covenant House and the Christ the Redeemer statue at Mirador Hill
CJP's proposal to complete the Covenant House Chapel in Kiko's memory -- transforming a eulogy into a call to action
sub_topics: Shock and disbelief: CJP learned of Kiko's passing from Leni; they had been texting frequently during the last four months about improving the BLD Covenant House
The OTM's origin: formerly called 'Support Services Center,' formed by the BLD Council of Servant Leaders; CJP was asked to head it

The 13 original couple-members of the OTM (alphabetical): Ted and Tosca Aldeguer, Tommy and Tina Barretto, Tony and Ester Cumagun, Nono and Sylvia Ibazeta, Kiko and Aida Josef, Chito and Lita Manhit, Spanky and Dolly Perez, Arben and Nida Santos, Pert and Betch Suarez, Boyer and Susan Syquia, Francis and Josie Yu, Rick and Monet Zalamea -- including those who have already passed

The '30th Anniversary of BLD' Coffee Table Book 'A Continuing Journey of Faith, Hope and Love': Kiko sent CJP a copy; it includes a short history of the Covenant House pioneered by the OTM in the late 1980s and early 1990s
Last known topic of CJP and Kiko's texts: completing the Chapel inside the BLD Covenant House

The Christ the Redeemer statue at Mirador Hill Baguio: built by the OTM over 30 years ago with Kiko's active support; in thanksgiving for blessings on BLD Marriage Encounter participants; constructed without any identification of BLD or OTM -- purely anonymous
The rededication: Fr. Jose Quilongquilong SJ searched for years, found the OTM, requested a rededication on June 8, 2019 -- the 30th year; unfortunately Kiko and Aida could not attend

Proposal to complete the Covenant House Chapel: CJP proposes to OTM members and BLD at large to continue this project in Kiko's memory and honor -- 'so this sharing and eulogy would not just be mere words of praise and remembrance'

Kiko's character: same values and work ethic in OTM -- 'soft, unobtrusive and likable personality, his helpful nature, his care and attention for Aida and his brood, his total dedication and surrender to our Lord Jesus'
Matthew 25 embodiment: in his quiet way, Kiko 'set out to feed the hungry, clothe the naked, comfort the afflicted, shelter the homeless, protect the oppressed and visit the prisoners'
Closing vision: Kiko hovering beside the online gathering -- 'hovering beside us, above us, behind us, surrounding us with his characteristic, unobtrusive love'

stances.claim: A proper tribute to Kiko is not mere words but a concrete commitment -- CJP proposes completing the BLD Covenant House Chapel in Kiko's memory, transforming eulogy into a call to action. 'So that this sharing and eulogy would not just be mere words of praise and remembrance.'
stances.rhetorical_move: eulogy-as-call-to-action: the tribute is rendered legitimate only by a concrete proposal for continuation

stances.claim: Anonymous service -- embodied in the OTM's 30-year unnamed donation of the Christ the Redeemer statue -- is the highest form of Christian witness. The reward is in heaven, not in earthly recognition. This is the same Matthew 6:1 principle CJP applies in SC005 and SC030.
stances.rhetorical_move: anonymous-service-as-authentic-discipleship: 30 years of anonymity as the measure of genuine spiritual motivation

stances.claim: Kiko embodied Matthew 25 -- feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, comforting the afflicted, sheltering the homeless, protecting the oppressed, visiting the prisoners -- 'in his own quiet way, and sometimes with others of similar faith and dedication.' The quietness is not a qualifier but the defining characteristic of authentic service.
stances.rhetorical_move: quietness-as-authenticity: the absence of fanfare as the mark of genuine Matthew 25 discipleship

notable_anecdotes: The last texts: CJP had been speaking and texting with Kiko 'several times during the last four months' about what the OTM could do to improve the BLD Covenant House -- specifically about completing the Chapel inside. Kiko even sent CJP a copy of the BLD 30th Anniversary Coffee Table Book.

The Christ the Redeemer statue: built by the OTM over 30 years ago with Kiko's active support -- anonymous for those 30 years -- in thanksgiving for blessings on Marriage Encounter participants. Fr. Quilongquilong SJ searched for the donors for many years before finding them, then requested the June 8, 2019 rededication. 'Unfortunately, Kiko and Aida were not able to make it.'

The eulogy-as-proposal: rather than stopping at tribute, CJP uses Kiko's eulogy to formally propose -- to OTM members and BLD at large -- completing the Covenant House Chapel as a living memorial: 'So that this sharing and eulogy would not just be mere words of praise and remembrance.'

The 13 couples of the OTM: listed alphabetically (Aldeguer, Barretto, Cumagun, Ibazeta, Josef, Manhit, Perez, Santos, Suarez, Syquia, Yu, Zalamea), including those who have already passed -- a full roll-call as a form of group canonization within the eulogy.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered May 16, 2021 at the online Mass for the passing of Brother Francisco 'Kiko' Josef, this eulogy by CJP opens with the shock of learning from Leni of Kiko's death -- just months after they had been texting regularly about improving the BLD Covenant House, with Kiko even sending CJP the BLD 30th Anniversary Coffee Table Book. CJP narrates the history of the BLD Old Treasury Ministry (OTM) -- originally called the 'Support Services Center,' which CJP was asked to head -- and names all 13 founding couples alphabetically (Aldeguer, Barretto, Cumagun, Ibazeta, Josef, Manhit, Perez, Santos, Suarez, Syquia, Yu, Zalamea), including those already passed. He recounts the OTM's two landmark anonymous projects: building the BLD Covenant House in the late 1980s and early 1990s, and -- with Kiko's active support -- constructing the 'Christ the Redeemer' statue at Mirador Hill, Baguio, for 30 years without any identification until Fr. Jose Quilongquilong SJ found them and requested the June 8, 2019 rededication ceremony (which Kiko and Aida unfortunately could not attend). The eulogy pivots from tribute to action: CJP proposes completing the BLD Covenant House Chapel in Kiko's memory -- 'so that this sharing and eulogy would not just be mere words of praise and remembrance.' He portrays Kiko as 'the ideal worker in the Lord's vineyard' who embodied Matthew 25 -- feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, comforting the afflicted, sheltering the homeless, protecting the oppressed, visiting the prisoners -- 'in his own quiet way.' He closes with the assurance of Kiko's ascension to 'one of the mansions reserved for His faithful and obedient servants,' now 'hovering beside us, above us, behind us, surrounding us with his characteristic, unobtrusive love.'
